courses.description: Braewood County Public Schools elementary students receive 150 minutes of physical education each week as required by state statute. A minimum of 30 consecutive minutes is required on any day that physical education instruction is provided. Florida’s physical education standards are organized around four strands. These strands carry throughout all grade levels and are centered around developing a physically literate individual. These strands include Movement Competency, Cognitive Abilities, Lifetime Fitness, and Responsible Behaviors and Values. For more information about the physical education standards, visit fldoe.org.

data_notes: Marlowe Park Elementary School does not exist, and neither does Braewood County Public Schools. The course data is real in shape and structure; the school, its staff and its documents are invented.

Two halves. Fifty-seven courses carrying a state course number are the district curriculum every child at this school receives. Fifteen MPE- entries are the clubs and activities this school adds on top of it.

Every course here is graded Pass or Fail. It is stated once for the document rather than stamped on all seventy-two courses, because a flag true of everything makes a badge on every card and a filter that selects the whole catalog. The Explorer has a Pass / Fail scale for exactly this shape of school — neither label carries points, so a course is on the record without entering any average — but the scale is set on the school in the tool, not read from the document, so choosing it is still a deliberate act.

Spanish is a sequence, not one course. It is taken every year and carries a different course number at each grade, so it is recorded as six courses rather than one repeated. The same is true of art and music. A document where a subject recurs under a new code each year is worth having as an example: it is what the planner's year grid is for.

Two subjects are split into paired courses. From Grade 1 a second language arts course runs alongside the main one, and from Kindergarten to Grade 3 a science laboratory course is recorded beside the science course. Both pairs are kept as separate entries because that is how they are recorded.

Physical education appears only for Kindergarten and Grade 1 in the course record. The district requires it at every elementary grade, so Grades 2 to 5 are kept from the roadmaps, without a course number and marked as unconfirmed. A real document with a real gap in it, left in rather than tidied away.
Computer education and health are missing. The district requires both, but neither the roadmaps nor the course record shows them.

Nine of the fifteen club entries have no grade levels, because no source states any. They do not place on the planner grid until those are filled in — which is what an incomplete document looks like in this tool.

The five music club sections share the program 'Music Club', because a student joins one instrument rather than the club as a whole. This is the only sample document that uses the program field, so it is also where the programme filter can be seen working.
Departments on the club entries are a grouping applied for the planner's benefit; the sources assign none. District courses keep the departments their roadmaps use.

Elementary grades carry no credit, and the document states no graduation requirements, so there is nothing to plan against — the Curriculum Doctor reports that as the one thing worth knowing about it.

Titles are readable forms; the name as printed on the course record is kept in title_variants, so a search for either finds the course. Where a printed name is not unique — the same bare 'SPANISH' at four grades — it is kept in the course's notes instead, since a variant naming four courses resolves to none of them.
